slides.title: Scaling Laws for Majority-based Opinion Dynamics in the Presence of Stubborn Agents
slides.tldr: PHASE TRANSITIONS IN OPINION DYNAMICS WITH STUBBORN AGENTS
slides.highlight: This research analyzes how stubborn agents influence opinion distribution and convergence time in multi-agent networks, which is relevant to MIMIC's societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Analyzes how stubborn agents influence opinion consensus time and steady-state distributions in majority-based networks.
card.key_idea: Uses a 2k-choices rule to identify three regimes (sub-critical, super-critical, critical) where mixing times are exponential, logarithmic, or polynomial in network size.
card.evaluation: Theoretically derived scaling laws were numerically validated by solving forward Kolmogorov and detailed balance equations for mixing times.
card.limitation: The analysis is limited to fully connected networks of agents.

slides.title: Locomotion Variability and User Experience in Smart Wheelchair Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: VARIABILITY-PRESERVING SHARED CONTROL IN SMART WHEELCHAIRS
slides.highlight: This research explores how preserving natural movement variability in shared control for smart wheelchairs increases user agency and usefulness. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: Preserving natural human movement variability in smart wheelchair assistance improves perceived agency and user experience.
card.key_idea: An autonomy-supportive shared control strategy that uses an inverted bell-shaped variability factor to minimize assistance in task-irrelevant areas while maintaining guidance at critical task points.
card.evaluation: User study with 18 participants pushing an intelligent powered wheelchair; measured via trajectory variance, endpoint error, and Likert-scale questionnaires (SoA, QUEAD2, UEQ).

slides.title: D3D-GEN: Robot-Aware Domain-Grounded Interactive 3D World Generation for Social Robotics
slides.tldr: INTERACTIVE 3D WORLD GENERATION FOR SOCIAL ROBOTICS
slides.highlight: D3D-GEN uses a RAG pipeline to automate the creation of interactive 3D simulation environments for social navigation. This supports RwB by providing realistic, domain-grounded worlds for training and validating embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: D3D-GEN generates interactive, robot-aware 3D simulation worlds grounded in autonomously retrieved domain-specific knowledge.
card.key_idea: A RAG pipeline uses a domain agent to collect real-world constraints, which then guide an LLM to synthesize floorplans and asset placements for simulators like Isaac Sim.
card.evaluation: Generated 450 worlds across residential, office, and hospital domains; outperformed baselines (e.g., ProcTHOR, DiffuScene) in object density, visual quality, and VQA accuracy.
card.limitation: Relies on an existing 3D asset database, which may not be available for every target domain.

slides.title: Avalon-ToM-Bench: Evaluating Fine-Grained Theory of Mind via Asymmetric Game Mechanics
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING THEORY OF MIND VIA ASYMMETRIC GAME MECHANICS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark to evaluate fine-grained Theory of Mind (ToM) and finds that robust ToM depends on learned reasoning policies rather than test-time deliberation, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of inferring partner intent via ToM.

card.one_liner: Avalon-ToM-Bench evaluates LLM Theory of Mind using asymmetric-information mechanics from the game The Resistance: Avalon.
card.key_idea: A 2x2 taxonomy (Epistemic/Motivational vs. Inference/Action) using perspective-constrained queries to decouple mental-state reasoning from general game-playing heuristics and rule knowledge.
card.evaluation: 28 LLMs were tested on 408 binary items. Results show models often represent correct inferences internally (via linear probing) but fail to express them.
card.limitation: Based on a single game, uses a binary verification format, and mechanistic probing was limited to open-weight Qwen3 models.

slides.title: THRIVE: Therapeutic Humanoid Robot In Virtual Environment
slides.tldr: ROBOT-ASSISTED REHABILITATION PLATFORM FOR CHILDREN
slides.highlight: This platform integrates virtual-reality games with a socially interactive robot therapist to support upper-limb rehabilitation for children. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction for therapeutic intervention.

card.one_liner: THRIVE is a modular at-home VR rehabilitation platform for children with upper-limb motor impairments.
card.key_idea: Integrates VR games, camera-based motion tracking, and a robot-agnostic therapist agent providing adaptive feedback to guide functional reaching and grasping movements.

slides.title: Study Explores Impact on Trust When Expressive Humanoid Robots Make Mistakes
slides.tldr: TRUST IMPACT OF HUMANOID ROBOT ERRORS
slides.highlight: This study examines how expressive humanoid robots affect user trust when mistakes occur, providing insights for the development of social robots in the RwB project.

slides.title: Multi-Agent AI Safety as an Institutional Design Problem
slides.tldr: AI SAFETY VIA INSTITUTIONAL DESIGN
slides.highlight: This research examines how institutional rules and authority states influence the safety and collective behavior of multi-agent systems, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: AI safety depends on institutional design, specifically how rules are communicated and how authority is tracked.
card.key_idea: Comparing constitutional prompts, local guards, and provenance-aware guards to show that identical violation rates can mask different mechanisms of behavioral prevention versus mechanical containment.
card.evaluation: 5,280 episodes across four model families using structured delegation workflows and resource-allocation tasks; results show provenance guards prevent laundering violations that local guards admit.
card.limitation: Synthetic, small-scale environments with limited action languages; results may not generalize to open-ended dialogue or complex real-world tool-use.

slides.title: X2-Turn: Frame-Synchronous Dual-Head Modeling for Joint Streaming ASR and Turn State Prediction
slides.tldr: FRAME-SYNCHRONOUS TURN STATE PREDICTION
slides.highlight: X2-Turn enables real-time distinction between interruptions, backchannels, and utterance completions, supporting HyECHO's goals in addressee/listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: X2-Turn enables joint, frame-synchronous streaming ASR and turn state prediction using a dual-head architecture.
card.key_idea: Extends Voxtral Realtime with a parallel turn state head sharing causal decoder representations, using ASR-anchored supervision to align word-level labels to 80ms frames.
card.evaluation: Tested on bilingual EasyTurn sets against cascaded and streaming baselines; showed superior accuracy-latency trade-offs and competitive ASR performance.
card.limitation: Joint training introduces some set-dependent degradation in ASR quality compared to ASR-only training.

slides.title: Hippocratic AI rolls out platform to coordinate teams of conversational voice AI agents
slides.tldr: COORDINATION OF CONVERSATIONAL VOICE AI AGENTS
slides.highlight: This platform for coordinating teams of conversational voice AI agents is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and the state of hybrid human-AI teams.

slides.title: EgoPHI: Estimating Contact and Force from Egocentric Vision
slides.tldr: EGO-CENTRIC FORCE AND CONTACT ESTIMATION
slides.highlight: EgoPHI estimates dense 3D contact maps and force distributions from monocular RGB images, supporting the physics-based human proficiency estimation required for MOSAIC.

slides.title: Multi-Agent AI Systems: How Startups Are Building Teams of AI Agents in 2026
slides.tldr: MULTI-AGENT AI SYSTEMS DEVELOPMENT
slides.highlight: This exploration of multi-agent AI systems aligns with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation using agent models.

slides.title: Leading-Silence Augmentation and Multi-Stage Synthetic Supervision for the Second MLC-SLM Challenge
slides.tldr: MULTILINGUAL CONVERSATIONAL SPEECH MODELING
slides.highlight: This work addresses speaker diarization and recognition in unsegmented multilingual conversations, contributing to HyECHO's goals in identity recognition and diarization.

card.one_liner: Improves multilingual conversational speech diarization and understanding using leading-silence augmentation and synthetic QA supervision.
card.key_idea: Task 1 uses random leading-silence cropping and EMA training on VibeVoice-ASR-7B. Task 2 employs synthetic QA generation with silent-audio filtering and distribution-matched augmentation for Qwen3-Omni-30B.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MLC-SLM Challenge sets; Task 1 reduced tcpMER from 18.30% to 16.73%, and Task 2 increased accuracy from 78.0% to 86.0%.
card.limitation: Ablations are cumulative, preventing independent estimation of EMA effects or uniform performance analysis across different languages and recording durations.

slides.title: Enabling Scalable Kinesthetic Teaching via Observer-based Hand-guiding with Active Support
slides.tldr: ACTIVE SUPPORT FOR KINESTHETIC TEACHING
slides.highlight: The proposed RHOAS scheme reduces operator fatigue and physical effort during hand-guiding via model-based force estimation, supporting the MOSAIC goal of improving human proficiency and skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: RHOAS enables effortless robot hand-guiding using observer-based force estimation to actively support human-intended motions.
card.key_idea: A control scheme using momentum-based external torque estimation, low-pass filtering, and a configuration-dependent confidence factor to provide active TCP velocity support without FT sensors.
card.evaluation: User study with 16 participants on KUKA LWR iiwa; measured human effort (energy), user preference, and task quality (precision/agility). Results showed statistically significant effort reduction.
card.limitation: The approach relies on an orthogonal projection to mitigate gravity compensation errors, which may limit support in the gravity vector direction.

slides.title: Diagnosis Before Recovery: Turning Agent Failures into Selective Self-Correction
slides.tldr: DIAGNOSIS-GUIDED SELECTIVE SELF-CORRECTION
slides.highlight: This work introduces DARC, a harness that profiles failure modes to apply selective recovery interventions, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction for reliable agent behavior.

card.one_liner: DARC improves agent self-correction by diagnosing failure modes to select targeted, cost-aware recovery interventions.
card.key_idea: It profiles development-set failures to restrict a recovery library to admissible interventions, then distills a frozen, success-cost policy for deployment to avoid irrelevant context and interference.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on ALFWorld, AppWorld, and XBRL Finance against baselines like ACE and MIPROv2; results show improved success and reduced environment steps/retrieval budgets.
card.limitation: The framework primarily evaluates controlled settings with one dominant failure mode per task family rather than learned per-instance routing.

slides.title: DuplexWorld: Can voice agents help you get through the day?
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING SPEECH-TO-SPEECH VOICE AGENTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces DuplexWorld to evaluate voice agents across diverse conversational scenarios, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement in human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: DuplexWorld is a holistic benchmark evaluating voice agents across conversational dynamics, agentic capability, and speech naturalness.
card.key_idea: A unified evaluation suite testing voice agents across six diverse worlds (enterprise and pathfinding) using 156 scenarios and eleven conversation types.
card.evaluation: Evaluated five commercial S2S systems using 12 metrics (e.g., Pass@1, DNSMOS). Results show a dissociation between conversational grace and task completion.
card.limitation: The benchmark uses simulated users rather than real human audio for its evaluations.

slides.title: Enhancing Virtual Agents through SLMs and Edge-Computing: An Exploratory Evaluation of Think and Memory Processes
slides.tldr: EDGE-BASED SLM FRAMEWORK FOR VIRTUAL AGENTS
slides.highlight: This research explores using Small Language Models (SLMs) and edge computing to implement cognitive processes like memory and reasoning for embodied virtual agents. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated interaction.

card.one_liner: Explores using Small Language Models on edge hardware to power cognitive processes for embodied virtual agents.
card.key_idea: Implements CEAA's 'Think' and 'Memory' processes using Qwen2.5 SLMs on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX for service routing and structured factual memory handling.
card.evaluation: Tested 0.5B, 1.5B, and 3.0B models using 1,000 routing prompts and 250 memory pairs; 3.0B model showed highest accuracy but highest latency.
card.limitation: Conducted in a controlled test-bed without live 3D interaction; results limited to Qwen2.5 variants and a single edge hardware configuration.

slides.title: Curvature-Aware Zeroth-Order Optimization for Memory-Efficient Test-Time Adaptation
slides.tldr: MEMORY-EFFICIENT TEST-TIME ADAPTATION VIA CURVATURE-AWARE ZO OPTIMIZATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces CAZO, a zeroth-order optimization method for test-time adaptation that reduces memory overhead by avoiding backpropagation. It is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of creating AI teammates that adapt at test time.

card.one_liner: CAZO improves memory-efficient test-time adaptation using curvature-aware zeroth-order optimization to reduce gradient estimation variance.
card.key_idea: Leverages a sliding-average diagonal Hessian estimation to perform anisotropic perturbation sampling, exploiting the low-rank and slow-varying curvature of the loss landscape during adaptation.
card.evaluation: Tested on ImageNet-C, R, V2, and Sketch using ViT-B/16; outperformed BP-based and BP-free baselines in accuracy and memory efficiency.
card.limitation: Performance depends on the number of perturbations (k), which linearly increases the number of required forward passes and runtime.

slides.title: SkillEvo: Self-Renewing Evolution Gradients from Multi-Turn Interaction Feedback
slides.tldr: SELF-RENEWING AGENT SKILL EVOLUTION VIA MULTI-TURN FEEDBACK
slides.highlight: SkillEvo introduces a method for evolving agent skills using multi-turn user simulation and a governance layer to repair degradation. This is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on agents that adapt and self-correct to improve human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: SkillEvo uses multi-turn interaction feedback and structural governance to continuously evolve agent skills in cloud services.
card.key_idea: It recasts multi-turn user simulation as a feedback generator to expose latent defects, paired with a governance layer that repairs factual degradation and structural bloat.
card.evaluation: Tested on 9 Tencent Cloud production skills; surpassed self-reflection by 23.0 and single-turn QA by 15.4 points in Task Success Rate (TSR).
card.limitation: Requires human confirmation before production rollout to mitigate risks of erroneous automatic revisions being served to users.

slides.title: Are You Aware of These 7 Reasons Why Multi-Agent Systems Are the Future of Agentic AI?
slides.tldr: MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS FOR AGENTIC AI
slides.highlight: This discussion on multi-agent systems is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation using agent models.

slides.title: FlowLOB: Efficient and Controllable Limit Order Book Generation with Flow Matching
slides.tldr: EFFICIENT LIMIT ORDER BOOK GENERATION VIA FLOW MATCHING
slides.highlight: FlowLOB utilizes flow-matching to generate realistic and controllable limit order book trajectories, contributing to the simulation of complex societal-scale systems relevant to MIMIC.

card.one_liner: FlowLOB uses flow matching to generate realistic, controllable limit order book trajectories with high sampling efficiency.
card.key_idea: A conditional flow-matching generator using an adaLN-Zero transformer and tick-relative representation to enable multi-symbol training and zero-shot transfer to unseen instruments.
card.evaluation: Tested on HKEX symbols using Wasserstein-1, KS, KL, and JS metrics against agent-based and learned baselines; results show superior realism at high frequencies.
card.limitation: Performance and controllability degrade at coarser sampling frequencies (10s), where it no longer dominates marginal realism metrics.

slides.title: Robust Multi-Tier Infant-Centered Audio Understanding with Whisper via Structured Speaker Conditioning
slides.tldr: INFANT-CENTERED AUDIO TAGGING VIA STRUCTURED SPEAKER CONDITIONING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multi-tier audio tagger using a speaker-aware Transformer to handle domain shifts and noise in home environments, contributing to HyECHO's goals in multimodal social perception and identity recognition.

card.one_liner: A multi-tier audio tagging framework for infant-centered recordings using a LoRA-finetuned Whisper encoder.
card.key_idea: Combines Whisper with a target-speaker-aware Transformer using factorized speaker tokens (shared tier token plus family-specific offset) and a sequence-level temporal smoothing loss for frame-level predictions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 17 hours of audio from 52 families using Macro-F1 and Kappa; outperformed TL-TR and W2V-LB baselines.
card.limitation: Unsupervised test-time adaptation for unseen families yielded only modest improvements, suggesting a need for more stable personalization mechanisms.

slides.title: Reinforcing Step-level Reasoning for Effective Self-Correction in LLMs
slides.tldr: STEP-LEVEL SELF-CORRECTION FRAMEWORK
slides.highlight: This work introduces SFS-DPO, a framework for step-level self-verification and self-correction, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and self-correction.

card.one_liner: SFS-DPO improves LLM math reasoning by training models to explicitly detect and correct step-level errors.
card.key_idea: A two-stage RL framework: first, step-level preference optimization strengthens reasoning; second, models learn to prefer self-corrected continuations over unaddressed errors, optionally using teacher-provided rationales (SFS-DPO-R).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 7 LLMs across MATH, GSM8K, GK2023, and OCW. Results show consistent accuracy gains over Step-DPO and SFT-based baselines.
card.limitation: SFS-DPO-R depends on teacher models, potentially propagating biases; effectiveness in non-mathematical, open-ended settings remains unexplored.
